title: Workflows and agents: who decides the next step

items.stem: The control flow is whatever decides which step runs next. In an agent loop, what decides after each tool result whether to call another tool or stop?

options.text: A fixed list of steps written by the developer in advance
The tool, which reports whether it needs one more call
The model, judging from the goal and the results so far
The student, who approves every step before it runs

items.stem: A fixed workflow always makes 2 model calls per request. An agent on the same requests averages 5 calls per request. Over 200 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make?
Every booking must run these steps in this order: check training status, check the calendar, book the slot, send a confirmation. For reliability and low cost, which design is best?

options.text: A fixed workflow, because the steps and their order never change
An agent, because booking needs the model's judgment at every step
An agent, because bookings matter too much for fixed steps
A fixed workflow, because a model cannot be used inside one

items.stem: Your program makes one model call that labels a question "manual" or "booking", then runs the matching fixed steps. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: An agent, because the model writes the steps that then run
An agent, because any program that calls a model is one
An agent, because the model reads the question and acts
A workflow, because the program fixes the steps after the label

items.stem: A student writes, "My 3D print keeps warping and I don't know why." Which design is most likely to find the cause?

options.text: A fixed workflow, because every question should follow the same steps
An agent, because each check's result decides which check comes next
A fixed workflow, because a long enough list covers every problem
An agent, because more model calls give better answers

items.stem: Policy says the training-status check must happen before every booking, with no exceptions. Should the model or the code own that step? Answer with one word.
